method: UNSD correspondence and SKOS whole/narrower mapping; source-based regressions, no applicable reference benchmark. See DESIGN.md.
biomassFindings: EIA-63C covers U.S. densified wood fuels, a component of biofuels; no wood qualifier is authorized.
Tables 2-8 distinguish manufacturing capacity, raw-material purchases, production, inventory, domestic sales and export sales.
Domestic price combines retail and wholesale sales; export price is revenue per ton.
Monthly capacity excludes planned and annually reporting small facilities; published capacity is annual tons per year, while API units say tons.
Feedstock purchases and their cost are manufacturing inputs, not fuel output or consumer fuel prices.

notation.action: Preserve nonnumeric under owner notation decision; never infer numeric zero.

crudeFindings: Company-level imports omit estimates included in broader aggregate imports; do not obtain the broader total by summing company records.
Origin countries are U.S. trade partners, not subject-country imports. Port-state and processing-state destinations are different bases.
Five advertised grade definitions are components of crude oil; absence of a grade filter does not prove an all-grade aggregate.
Crude remains a component of petroleum; an all-crude measure may only enter the separately counted explicit crude-oil qualifier cells after scope/availability checks.
invariants: Every original column/facet definition is retained.
Every grade is a crude component, even where destination is national.
No source components become whole products through headline fallback.
No implicit summation, computed totals or substitution.
